text.p: The following stories were reported in Lithuanian newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- After meeting Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius, World Bank representatives praised the efforts of the government to reform the energy and banking sectors and urged speeding up pension reform.
- Hermis Bank intends to acquire 51 percent stake in regional Siauliu Bank.
- President Algirdas Brazauskas encouraged representatives of J.P. Morgan Securities and other foreign investors to invest more intensively during a meeting.
- Economists forecast that the rise of the minimum salary to 400 litas will increase unemployment.
- Vilniaus Bank plans to develop further its leasing and credit card business and take part in the privatisation of state run Commercial Bank.
- The 10 biggest Lithuanian breweries produced 25.54 million litres of beer in the first quarter of 1997, 3 million litres more than in the same period last year.
- Journalists are encountering barricades erected by high-ranking officials. Defence Minister Cheslovas Stankevichius has imposed strict rules on providing information.
- The government decided on Wednesday to change ambassadors in Finland, Kazakhstan, France, Belarus, Finland, Estonia, Sweden, the U.S. and NATO.

- Eurominister Laima Andrikiene said the applications for a bid to draw up a privatisation program for Lithuanian Telecom should be submitted by May 9. She also said the privatisation of the state-run telephone operator may start next spring.
- The increase of excise duties on fuel will push up the prices of food products.
- The government wants a transparent and fair privatisation process.
